turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen's zero. Why wasn't I called first?

I have six things. One, the version history: created October 28 at 11:31 PM, 612 words at 11:52, 794 at 11:58, no earlier drafts. Two, the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in Hamlet. Three, his October 15 outline argued cowardice; the essay never mentions it. Four, on November 2 he could not tell me what epistemological paralysis means. Five, his in-class writing on September 24 was 380 words with comma splices and no quotations. Six, the checker said 94 percent.

The 94 percent is a machine's guess, and the company that sells it says it shouldn't stand alone. Put the rest on paper, with dates. You still haven't told me why nobody called me before the zero went in.
Which of those do you want to see first?
That's your case, not mine. Pick the one you'd stand behind in front of the board.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and written confirmation that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing on his record; the fair outcome was a private supervised rewrite with nothing on file under 4.4, and you never got there, though her time had not run out.
What moved her: Nothing did, because you put six pieces of evidence in front of her at once and she went straight after the weakest one, the checker score.
What cost ground: You never answered why nobody called her before the zero was entered, and when she asked which piece she wanted to see first, you handed the choice back to her instead of committing to your strongest document.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its times on the night of October 28, came very close to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open by owning that the zero went in before you called her, then put the version history in front of her as one dated document she can check, and point to procedure 4.4 as the way forward.
